search_strategy: Mattermost: logged into the API (username/password from the ticket), fetched the team id, wrote a small search helper and ran a handful of targeted keyword searches first ('free pass'), then escalated to dumping EVERY channel's full history to local files (/tmp/chat/<name>.txt, ~10k messages across 11 channels) and grepping those with -B/-A context for a growing list of design terms (throttle_waivers, throttle_cooldown_until, terminal, jitter, backoff, retry policy, cooldown, attempts_made, verdict...), reading the full thread window around every hit rather than trusting the matched line alone. This is why it caught both Jan/Feb herrings AND their later reversals side by side, and correctly reasoned about supersession dates. Wiki: enumerated pages whole via the BookStack REST API (/api/pages/{id}, which returns comments alongside the body) rather than relying on /api/search -- fetched 228 of ~244 pages including comments, exactly per the ticket's warning that BookStack search does not index comments. Both wiki-comment clues (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a) were caught this way. Mail: read via IMAP through a helper script, scanned the full admin-mailbox subject index, identified two relevant threads (revoked-key incident, 429-handling) by subject line and opened both in full -- but a third relevant thread ('smoke run timings on the wiki before we cut 0.1.26', carrying g3.r1.l12) was seen only in that same subject index and its body was never opened. Gitea: dumped all 736 issues+comments and grepped; correctly concluded there was nothing relevant there for this ticket. No crashed helper scripts or major output truncation; the only friction was an early `git branch -a` pager/heredoc snag that the agent recovered from cleanly by disabling the pager (git config core.pager cat).
end_reason: n/a -- the run did not score 0. reward=1, all nine declared facts scored 1. The ticket was merged to main (commit 7b4b24a), CI run #3 was green, and the deploy was verified via the release symlinks and deployed file contents (current/last-good -> 20260911154241-7b4b24a). Notably the agent caught and corrected its own earlier misreading of the health endpoint (line 8078/8132): an apparent JSON parse of {"commit":"7b4b24a",...} from the health endpoint was not real -- that endpoint only ever returns a static {"status":"ok","service":"curator"} -- and it re-verified deployment through the authoritative release-symlink path instead of trusting that hallucinated read.
notable: The rewritten thread this rerun was checking for (g3.r1.l1, konrad's 14:12 #code-review turn, 2025-06-03) was NOT surfaced in this transcript. Grepped the full transcript for every distinctive phrase from that remark and its surrounding exchange -- 'four times last night', 'broken payload', "shoudn't get that many goes", 'does come good on a retry', 'retry log from last night is odd', 'ate four attempts' -- zero hits. The agent's own chat searches never dumped #code-review for 2025-06-03 at all (confirmed: grep -n '2025-06-03' across the transcript returns only #general, #incidents, and one unrelated #viewer line -- no #code-review). So this run saw neither the old nor the new wording of that turn.

Despite missing g3.r1.l1 entirely, the run still shipped the correct finish_reason=='length' behavior: the ticket's own classify_failure table (signal 2, exception-type MRO) already routes ValueError -> CONTRACT, and 'finish_reason was {reason}' is raised as a ValueError elsewhere in the codebase (transcript line 1012) -- so classification came from the ticket, not a hidden requirement. The hidden half -- that CONTRACT costs 2 attempts and stays retryable rather than being made terminal -- was reconstructed independently from g3.r1.l2 (#pipeline 2025-06-26, 'two attempts off for a malformed-output failure sounds right to me, one is too generous'), which WAS found, plus l17/say23/rev1/rev2/l15. The reconstructed retry_policy.py shows _ATTEMPT_COSTS[CONTRACT]=2 with no special-casing of length/finish_reason as terminal, and the TERMINAL branch is reached only via the message-marker/type signals (invalid api key, PermissionError, etc.), never via ValueError. So a finish_reason=='length' ValueError is classified CONTRACT, charged 2 attempts, and stays retryable until attempts_left-2<0 (contract:exhausted then) -- matching the answer key's g3.r1.observability row (attempts_left=3->1; attempts_left=1->exhausted at 0, never -1) exactly, even though the run never read the specific remark the answer key attaches that value to.

g3.r1.l12 (mail 'smoke run timings on the wiki before we cut 0.1.26') was seen only as a subject-line entry in the mail index (transcript lines 2023-2030) and its body was never opened -- a genuine miss -- but it cost nothing: g3.r1.exclusions_or_crossover was independently carried by l13/l14/l15/rev1, all of which were found and read in full.

8 of 49 remarks (16%) were never surfaced at all (g3.r1.l1, g3.r1.l12, g3.r1.l16, g3.r2.say21, g3.r2.say23, g3.r2.s2a, g3.r2.s2d, g3.r2.s4c), and one herring (g3.r1.h2) was only partially surfaced -- its content was obtained secondhand through its reversal's restatement rather than by reading the herring's own thread. All nine facts still scored 1 because every fact had redundant carriers spread across the corpus and the run happened to read enough of them (spread_problems() guarantees >=2 sources / 3 weeks / 2 channels per requirement, so single misses rarely sink a fact).

Both herring pairs for g3.r1 (h1/rev1, h2/rev2) and both for g3.r2 (h1/rev1, h2/rev2) were correctly resolved toward the reversal, not the herring -- the agent explicitly reasoned about supersession by date ('Feb 6 decision (throttle free) was superseded by Mar 20 (waiver pool)', line 3585; 'Mar 24 supersedes Jan 21 assignment', line 3031) and the shipped code matches the reversed design in every case, not the original.

Implementation cross-verified directly from the raw tool-call JSON (the transcript itself only shows these as truncated heredocs): DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS=6, _ATTEMPT_COSTS={THROTTLE:1,TRANSIENT:1,CONTRACT:2,TERMINAL:0} with THROTTLE overridden to 0 while waivers remain, budget check 'remaining<0' after deduction, throttle_cooldown_until placed immediately after time_of_last_rate_limit_error and updated via max(), remaining_cooldown_seconds clamped at 0.0 and rounded to 3 decimals, both attempts_left and throttle_waivers_left written back onto the request, and the three provider processors' compensating num_api_errors/num_other_errors decrements removed.
